q: You want to install Proxmox inside a VM on ACE. Which setting must be enabled?
why: Nested Proxmox needs hardware-assisted virtualization exposed to the guest.

q: Which network mode did the VirtualBox Ubuntu lab specify for internet access?
why: The lab specifies NAT for the Ubuntu VM's network adapter.

q: Which shortcut did the Windows Server lab use to enter Audit Mode at the initial setup screen?
why: Ctrl + Shift + F3 enters Audit Mode during the initial Windows setup experience.

q: You want a reusable standardized starting point for making more Windows Server VMs. What should you create?
why: The lab creates a Windows Server template and then clones from it.

q: A new virtual disk appears in Windows but cannot store files yet. What is the next step?
a: Initialize it, create a volume, format NTFS, assign a drive letter
Change the VM to bridged networking
why: The disk must be initialized, partitioned/formatted, and assigned a drive letter.

q: True or false: A Proxmox virtual bridge can act like a switch connecting VMs to each other or an external network when configured appropriately.
why: The lab describes bridges as switch-like connections for VM networking.

q: For internal-only vmbr1 in Lab 3b, what IPv4/CIDR setting is specified?
why: The lab says to leave IPv4/CIDR blank for internal network use.

q: Two VMs on an internal bridge have no DHCP server. What should you do?
a: Assign static IPs in the same subnet
Increase both VMs to four CPU cores
why: The lab requires static IP addresses in the same subnet for this internal network.

q: Which command tests connectivity between two VMs?
why: The lab asks students to ping between the VMs.

q: Which Proxmox bridge is configured for VLAN tagging in Lab 3b?
a: A bridge with a drive letter
why: The lab specifies vmbr2 with VLAN-aware checked.

q: Which item is NOT one of the three storage technologies covered in your Proxmox storage lab?
why: The lab covers DAS, NAS, and SAN. DNS resolves names and is not a storage technology.

q: Which filesystem does the Proxmox local-das directory-storage exercise specify?
why: The lab specifies ext4 for local-das.

q: Which feature lets a VM access a folder on the host computer?
why: The lab configures shared folders and accesses them from the guest.

q: True or false: Assigning more vCPUs to a VM always improves performance.
why: Extra vCPUs can hurt performance depending on host resources and CPU contention.

q: Which configuration matches the suggested lightweight Puppy Linux VM in Proxmox?
a: 1 GB disk, 1 CPU core, 512 MB–1 GB RAM
why: The assignment suggests a 1 GB disk, 1 core, and 512 MB–1 GB RAM.

q: What is memory ballooning used for?
a: Reclaiming unused memory from a VM when needed elsewhere
why: Ballooning reclaims unused guest memory when the host needs it elsewhere.

q: A VM is allocated 4 GB of RAM. What can its guest OS use under that allocation?
a: The memory allocated to the VM, subject to its configuration
why: A VM sees and uses the memory allocated to it, subject to its configuration.

q: Which storage technique replaces duplicate entities with pointers to the original?
why: The storage slides describe deduplication as replacing duplicates with pointers to original data.

q: What is the key trade-off with thin provisioning?
a: All disk space is reserved immediately
Space is not fully pre-allocated, so actual storage use must be monitored
The VM can never run out of storage
It doubles the VM's CPU count
why: Thin provisioning does not pre-allocate all capacity, but underlying storage can fill.

q: VirtualBox is which type of hypervisor in your course material?
a: Type 2, running on a host operating system
why: The course slides classify VirtualBox as a Type 2 hypervisor.

q: Your Proxmox web interface uses which port in the lab's example URL?
why: The Proxmox web interface is shown at https://IP:8006.

q: You need to upload a Linux ISO into Proxmox before creating a VM. Where does the lab direct you?
a: Node > Local storage > ISO Images > Upload
why: The assignment uploads the ISO through Local storage's ISO Images tab.

q: In the Windows virtual disk lab, which partition style did the initialization prompt specify?
why: The lab says to select GPT when initializing the new disk.

q: A host folder is shared with a VirtualBox Windows guest. Which path format does the lab give for accessing a shared folder?
why: The lab gives the VirtualBox shared-folder path as \\vboxsrv\[shared_folder_name].

q: A VM is slow and the host is experiencing CPU contention. What is the best first principle from the CPU slides?
a: Add vCPUs to every VM immediately
Start with a modest vCPU allocation and increase only if needed
why: The slides recommend starting with one vCPU and increasing if needed; more vCPUs are not always better.

q: Which Microsoft utility is used to automate customization of a Windows Server installation?
why: The Test-1 questions identify Sysprep as the Microsoft utility used to automate Windows Server customization.

q: What is the default port number for the Proxmox web interface?
why: The Test-1 questions identify port 8006 as the default Proxmox web-interface port.

q: Which statement describes a Type 1 hypervisor?
a: It runs on top of a host operating system
It runs directly on the server hardware
It is a virtual disk format
why: The Test-1 questions distinguish Type 1 hypervisors as running directly on server hardware.

q: Which feature lets you return a virtual machine to an earlier point in time?
why: The Test-1 questions identify snapshots as the feature for returning a VM to a prior state.

q: In a bridged network configuration, how do virtual machines appear on the network?
a: They can have unique IP addresses visible to the external network
They can communicate only with host services
They are always assigned a new IP after every reboot
why: The Test-1 questions describe bridged VMs as having unique network IP addresses visible from outside the host.
